_comment: Worked example of the Sixth Form content format (docs/SPEC-SIXTH-FORM.md § 11). Level 6 and the briefs only. Not loaded by the site: the real file will be src/content/lessons/02-web-app/lesson.json.
title: My web app
summary: Build a working web app in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, then read, fix and trace code you didn't write.

briefs.name: Password checker
briefs.pitch: Score how strong a password is.
briefs.title: Password Checker

briefs.name: Grade calculator
briefs.pitch: Turn an exam mark into a grade.
briefs.title: Grade Calculator

briefs.name: Café order
briefs.pitch: Work out what an order costs, in pence.
briefs.title: Café Order

briefs.name: Unit converter
briefs.pitch: Convert between kilometres and miles, using 8 km = 5 miles.
briefs.title: Unit Converter

starter: <!-- Build your {brief} here. Start with the doctype. -->

levels.title: Make it respond
levels.intro: Your form does nothing yet. Add a script so the page responds when someone presses the button.

addFiles.script.js: // The JavaScript for your {brief} goes here.

given.code:
const form = document.getElementById("checker"); // given
form.onsubmit = function () { // given
  const value = form.{inputName}.value; // given

  return false; // given
}; // given

goals.text: Load script.js with a <script> tag at the end of the body
hints: script.js is a separate file, so the script tag needs a src attribute.
Put it just before </body>, so the form exists when the script runs.

goals.text: Write a function {fn} that returns the right answer
hints: Write the function above the given code, not inside it.
Start with a variable for the answer, change it with if statements, then return it.
In pseudocode this is function {fn}(…) … return … endfunction. JavaScript uses { } instead of endfunction.

goals.text: Show the answer inside #result using getElementById and innerHTML
goals.spec: 5d JS · output by changing an element
hints: First get hold of the element: chosenElement = document.getElementById("…"). Which id did you give the box in index.html?
Call {fn}(value) inside the given handler, before return false.

goals.text: Stretch: if the input is empty, warn the user with alert()
hints: An empty text box gives the empty string "".

challenges.title: Output to an element
challenges.question: The variable score holds a number. Write JavaScript that displays score in the HTML element with the id result.
markScheme: Uses document.getElementById("result") to get the element
Sets .innerHTML of that element to score (one statement is fine)
